summary: This bill requires all Department of Defense military personnel actions to be based exclusively on individual merit and prohibits any consideration of race, ethnicity, or national origin, with a narrow exception for combatant commander-approved taskings in specific unconventional foreign missions that must be reported to Congress.

scores.thoughts: The bill addresses military personnel policies regarding merit and racial neutrality but contains no provisions related to budgets, appropriations, or changes in government expenditure levels.
The bill makes no reference to tax policy, rates, or revenue measures of any kind.
No provisions in the bill concern healthcare systems, coverage, or delivery models.
The legislation does not address firearms regulations or Second Amendment issues.
The bill contains nothing related to immigration policy, borders, or pathways to citizenship.
No content in the bill pertains to reproductive rights or abortion access.
While the bill concerns Department of Defense personnel practices, it does not alter funding levels, procurement, or overall defense spending.
The bill has no environmental or climate-related provisions.
No elements of the bill affect welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety net policies.
The legislation does not address education policy, school funding, or choice programs.
The bill makes no mention of drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related policies.
No provisions relate to criminal sentencing, policing, or justice system reforms.
The bill does not engage with trade, tariffs, or globalization issues.
Nothing in the bill addresses deficit spending, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
The bill prohibits consideration of race, ethnicity, and national origin but does not address sexual orientation, gender identity, or LGBTQ+ legal protections.
The legislation contains no provisions on foreign aid or international assistance.
No content relates to voting access, election integrity, or electoral reforms.
The bill does not address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions concern labor rights, union power, or workplace regulations.

The bill focuses on prohibiting racial considerations in military personnel decisions but does not engage with religious exemptions or conflicts between religious liberty and anti-discrimination laws.
